Header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Nora Kim (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Stratagem Procurement), Maya Singh (Stratagem Head of Sec), Raj Patel (Stratagem VP Eng), Evelyn Park (Stratagem Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Procurement call focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA specifics, pricing approval path and pilot onboarding. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. quick intro — samira patel, account exec for stratagem, with diego our se and nora our csm.
[00:08] Liam: Hey thanks, Liam here — procurement, i'll be driving contract timeline.
[00:12] Maya: Maya, security. we'll want to dig into DPA and kms stuff.
[00:15] Raj: Raj, eng — we'll handle pilot and benchmarks.
[00:18] Evelyn: Evelyn from legal, i'll be reviewing the ms a, dpa redlines.
[00:23] Samira: Great. high-level agenda: align on redlines, SLA language (uptime, credits), pricing bands and next steps to get pilot running. Does that work?
[00:30] Maya: Yes. first question — data residency, we saw in the DPA there was mention of eu residency for european patients. we need clarification on where logs and pdbs live, is that configurable per customer?
[00:45] Diego: short answer: yes, for private and dedicated we can pin region and storage. for hosted API there's region controls and retention options. note: some transcribed docs may say "R D P" or "R V P C" but we support VPC peering and customer-managed s3. we also support bring-your-own-kms (BYOK) for private deployments.
[01:05] Maya: BYOK is critical. we need HSM-compatible KMS and key rotation logs. also, audit trails for model invocations — how long are those retained?
[01:15] Nora: Hey maya, we typically retain audit logs based on the customer's retention tier; standard is 90 days but enterprise can request 2 years for an additional fee. we'll include specifics in the SLA appendix.
[01:25] Raj: For the pilot, we'd like to run an on-prem/VPC deployment — synthetic workload, egress controls, and latency targets. we'll need a runbook.
[01:35] Diego: Absolutely. diego here — i'll own the pilot runbook. it'll include infra diagrams, required instance types, sequence lengths, and benchmark scripts. quick clarif: are you planning to use our Dedicated offering or fully private on-prem?
[01:48] Raj: We prefer private VPC for PHI concerns, but open to a short Dedicated pilot if it speeds up procurement.
[01:56] Samira: procurement note — often legal prefers seeing MSA + DPA together. Evelyn, did you send redlines already?
[02:03] Evelyn: we sent initial redlines last week. primary asks: stronger indemnification carveouts, narrower data processing scope, and a clearer SLA credit mechanism.
[02:14] Samira: good. on indemnity we can discuss limits tied to net sales, but we usually can't accept uncapped indemnity. on SLA credits — diego, can you describe how we measure uptime?
[02:25] Diego: Sure. monitoring is at the route/model level; we measure availability as successful token responses vs time, excluding scheduled maintenance windows. credits are pro-rated by outage minutes and applied as service credits on next invoice.
[02:38] Liam: Procurement: how are scheduled maint windows communicated? We need a 30-day notice for impacting changes.
[02:45] Nora: we typically give a 7-14 day notice for routine planned maintenance; for major infra changes we can agree to 30 days in the enterprise contract.
[02:55] Maya: Security: SOC2 report and ISO certs — do you have recent artifacts? where can we get them?
[03:02] Samira: yes, we'll share our latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary. link will be shared via the secure portal.
[03:09] Evelyn: On the DPA, we need explicit language on data deletion at contract termination and the certification process. also, subprocessors list is required.
[03:19] Samira: We'll include subprocessors and a deletion certification clause in the DPA appendix.
[03:24] Raj: About performance — what's the baseline latency we can expect for a 2k token generation in Dedicated vs quantized on-prem?
[03:33] Diego: rough numbers: hosted GPU with optimized kernels can do X 2k in ~300-400ms median under load for certain model families; Dedicated under reserved capacity gets more predictable p50/p95. On-prem varies by instance size and quantization — with int8 quant and proper kernels you can see similar latencies but we should run the benchmark. quick caveat — these numbers are model dependent and sequence dependent.
[03:57] Raj: okay we'll plan benchmarks. can you provide a sample benchmark spreadsheet?
[04:01] Samira: yes, will share pricing/benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:05] Liam: Pricing approvals — we need committed monthly spend tiers to route through procurement. what's typical contract length and discounting?
[04:14] Samira: common patterns: 12-month reserved for Dedicated with staged ramp and discount on committed commit levels. pricing spreadsheet will show usage vs unit price and enterprise discounts — we'll send one.
[04:23] Evelyn: Legal: SLA credit calculation must be machine-verifiable; also want a cap on credits so it's predictable.
[04:31] Diego: credits are deterministic based on outage minutes; we'll include formula in SLA appendix. cap is negotiable — typical is up to 50% of monthly fees for severe outages but we can discuss.
[04:45] Maya: Encryption at rest/in transit — we need TLS + customer-managed KMS for keys at rest, and separation of logs for PHI. how segregated are logs?
[04:54] Diego: logs can be directed to customer-managed buckets in VPC/S3. for Hosted we retain some aggregated telemetry in Redwood for platform ops, but PHI or payload-level logs are configurable and can be disabled.
[05:05] Raj: network egress — we need assurance that model weights won't be exfiltrated. can you outline controls?
[05:12] Diego: for private deployments, model weights sit in your environment and access is local; for Dedicated we use encrypted storage and RBAC to limit access. we'll include an architecture note.
[05:22] Samira: circling back to timeline — Liam, what internal approvals are needed?
[05:26] Liam: procurement committee needs pricing and SLA, legal needs MSA+DPA redlines, security needs SOC2 + KMS details. if we get those artifacts this week, target approvals in 2-3 weeks.
[05:36] Evelyn: legal will propose a few redlines; we need Redwood's position on arbitration and governing law.
[05:42] Samira: Redwood prefers arbitration in CA with mutual waiver, but we can discuss jurisdiction — we'll flag to legal.
[05:49] Maya: Also request for penetration test schedule and third-party attestation.
[05:53] Nora: we run periodic pentests and can provide attestation; for specific customer tests we can set a scoping call.
[05:58] Raj: ok pilot logistics: we'll need the runbook, a security checklist, and a timeline. propose pilot window 4 weeks with success criteria: throughput > X tps, p95 latency < Y ms, data residency & logging verified.
[06:15] Diego: I will draft the runbook with those criteria, include scripts, and the sample infra.
[06:22] Samira: Great. next steps recap?
[06:25] Liam: we need pricing + SLA spreadsheet, updated MSA+DPA with redlines, pilot runbook, SOC2 and KMS docs.
[06:31] Samira: We'll send: pricing/SLA (Samira), pilot runbook (Diego), SOC2 + certs (Nora), and legal team will get redlines back to Evelyn by 3/15.
[06:40] Evelyn: we'll review and revert.
[06:42] Samira: Alright thanks everyone — we'll follow up with slide pack and links.
[06:46] Liam: Thanks.
[06:48] Call ended.
